text: The question which the passage raises is, in its nature, unanswerable. Genesis 22 may be called a story of sacrifice; but it is still more a story about reading, and what is to be learned from it is that the most important things are those a text declines to say. Every such gap lays some demand upon the reader: the silence of Abraham, the question of Isaac, the absence of Sarah, and, last of all, the refusal of the narrator to explain.
